questions.question: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the diver against the stream is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the distance (50 km) is constant, the speed of the diver is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Time ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 2 : 1 ⇒ Speed ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 1 : 2

Speed in still water = (Upstream Speed + Downstream Speed) ÷ 2 = (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 ratio units.

We are given that still water speed is 3 km/h ⇒ 1.5 ratio units = 3 km/h.

⇒ 1 ratio unit = 2 km/h. Since the upstream speed corresponds to 1 ratio unit, it directly equals 2 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of diver in still water (v) = 3 km/h

Distance traveled upstream and downstream = 50 km

Time taken upstream = 2 × Time taken downstream

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = v − s | Downstream Speed = v + s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48f09262346862c9fff8b21985306db6d9d5a9a92aff7db86ea732a6b26b9e5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = (3 − s) km/h

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = (3 + s) km/h

According to the given condition in the question:

⇒ 50 ÷ (3 − s) = 2 × [50 ÷ (3 + s)]

Canceling 50 from both sides:

⇒ 1 ÷ (3 − s) = 2 ÷ (3 + s)

By cross-multiplying:

⇒ 3 + s = 2 × (3 − s)

⇒ 3 + s = 6 − 2s

⇒ s + 2s = 6 − 3

⇒ 3s = 3

⇒ s = 1 km/h

The speed of the diver against the stream (Upstream Speed):

⇒ U = 3 − s

⇒ U = 3 − 1 = 2 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: v = (D + U) ÷ 2, where D is downstream speed and U is upstream speed.

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: s = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Constant Distance Relation

Whenever the distance traveled is constant, the ratio of speeds is always inversely proportional to the ratio of their respective times taken. (Speed ∝ 1 ÷ Time).
</p

questions.question: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the diver downstream is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of diver in still water (u) = 3 km/h

Distance upstream = Distance downstream = 50 km

Time upstream is double the time downstream.

**Formula used:**

Speed downstream = u + v

Speed upstream = u - v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the stream be v km/h.

Time upstream = 2 × Time downstream

⇒ 50 ÷ (u - v) = 2 × (50 ÷ (u + v))

⇒ 50 ÷ (3 - v) = 2 × (50 ÷ (3 + v))

⇒ 1 ÷ (3 - v) = 2 ÷ (3 + v)

⇒ 3 + v = 2 × (3 - v)

⇒ 3 + v = 6 - 2v

⇒ 3v = 3

⇒ v = 1 km/h

Speed downstream = u + v = 3 + 1 = 4 km/h

**∴ The speed of the diver downstream is 4 km/h.**

questions.question: A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/hr, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 250 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial speed of the car = 275 km / 5 hr = 55 km/hr

Reduced speed of the car = 55 km/hr - 5 km/hr = 50 km/hr

Distance to be covered = 250 km

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Time taken to cover 250 km at 50 km/hr:

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 250 km / 50 km/hr

⇒ Time = 5 hours

**The car will take 5 hours to cover a distance of 250 km.**

questions.question: Sumit travelled 10 km 120 m by scooter, 1 km 970 m on foot and 15 km 850 m by bus. What is the total distance travelled by Sumit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance travelled by scooter = 10 km 120 m

Distance travelled on foot = 1 km 970 m

Distance travelled by bus = 15 km 850 m

**Formula Used:**

Total distance travelled = Distance by scooter + Distance on foot + Distance by bus

**Calculation:**

Convert all distances to meters:

Distance by scooter = 10 km 120 m = 10,120 m

Distance on foot = 1 km 970 m = 1,970 m

Distance by bus = 15 km 850 m = 15,850 m

Total distance travelled:

⇒ 10,120 m + 1,970 m + 15,850 m

⇒ 27,940 m

Convert the total distance back to km and meters:

27,940 m = 27 km 940 m

**The total distance travelled by Sumit is 27 km 940 m.**

questions.question: A 250 m long train running at a speed of 100 km/h crosses another train, coming from the opposite direction at a speed of 62 km/h, in 10 seconds. What is the length of the second train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of first train = 250 m

Speed of first train = 100 km/h

Speed of second train = 62 km/h

Time to cross each other = 10 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (when moving in opposite direction) = Speed of first train + Speed of second train

Distance = Relative speed × Time

Total Distance = Length of first train + Length of second train

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 100 km/h + 62 km/h

Relative speed = 162 km/h = 162 × (5/18) m/s = 45 m/s

Time = 10 seconds

Distance covered in 10 seconds = 45 m/s × 10 s = 450 m

Total Distance = Length of first train + Length of second train

450 m = 250 m + Length of second train

⇒ Length of second train = 450 m - 250 m = 200 m

**The length of the second train is 200 m.**

Speed = 72 × (5)/(18) 

Speed = 20 m/s

Length of the train = Speed × Time

Length of the train = 20 × 24

⇒ Length of the train = 480 m

**The length of the train is 480 m.**

questions.question: Two trains travelling in the same direction at 40 km/h and 22 km/h cross each other completely in 1 minute. If the length of the first train is 125 m, what is the length of the second train?

Distance covered (total length of both trains) = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance covered = 5 m/s × (1/60) hour × 3600 seconds/hour = 300 m

Total length of both trains = 300 m

Length of second train (L₂) = Total length - Length of first train

⇒ L₂ = 300 m - 125 m

⇒ L₂ = 175 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Two people drive towards each other from two places which are 56 km apart. The speed of the first person is 12 km/h and the speed of the other is 14 km/h. After how long will they be 4 km apart if they start driving at the same time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The distance between two places = 56 km

Speed of the first person = 12 km/h

Speed of the second person = 14 km/h

**Formula used:**

Relative speed = Speed of the first person + Speed of the second person

Time (t) = Distance / Relative speed

**Calculations:**

Relative speed = 12 km/h + 14 km/h = 26 km/h

They need to be 4 km apart, so the distance covered together = 56 km - 4 km = 52 km

Time (t) = 52 km / 26 km/h

⇒ t = 2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: A thief running at a speed of 8 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 10 km/h. If the thief is 100 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of policeman = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

Distance gap to close = 100 m = 0.1 km

Time required = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 0.1 ÷ 2 = 1/20 hours

Time in minutes = 1/20 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the policeman (Sₚ) = 10 km/h

Speed of the thief (Sₜ) = 8 km/h

Initial distance ahead (D) = 100 m = 0.1 km

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Sₚ − Sₜ (Since they move in the same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e608d9911945b0b381ea958572edfa19dc2c6160b6bab924db96c7070f4db41a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 − 8 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time required to catch the thief = 0.1 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.05 hours

⇒ To convert hours into minutes, multiply by 60:

⇒ Time required = 0.05 × 60 = 3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds S₁ and S₂ (where S₁ > S₂), their relative speed is S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other at speeds S₁ and S₂, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
</p

questions.question: A cyclist covers 2.5 km in 4 minutes 10 seconds. How long will he take to cover 6 km at the same speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered = 2.5 km

Time taken = 4 minutes 10 seconds = 4 + 10/60 minutes = 4 + 1/6 minutes = 25/6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 2.5 km / (25/6 minutes)

⇒ Speed = 2.5 × (6/25) km/minute

⇒ Speed = 0.6 km/minute

To find the time to cover 6 km:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 6 km / 0.6 km/minute

⇒ Time = 10 minutes

**The cyclist will take 10 minutes to cover 6 km at the same speed.**

questions.question: Rama walks to her office 5 km away from home. In the morning, she covers the distance in 1 hour whereas, while returning home in the evening, she takes 15 more minutes to cover the same distance. Find her average speed (in km/h) during the two-way journey.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance (d) = 5 km

Time taken in the morning (t₁) = 1 hour

Time taken in the evening (t₂) = 1 hour 15 minutes = 1.25 hours

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 5 km + 5 km = 10 km

Total time = 1 hour + 1.25 hours = 2.25 hours

⇒ Average speed = 10 km / 2.25 hours

⇒ Average speed = 4 (4)/(9) km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach the destination in 2 hrs, exactly on time. If I increase my speed by 5 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed = 10 km/h

Time = 2 hrs

Increased speed = 10 km/h + 5 km/h = 15 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Distance = 10 km/h × 2 hrs

Distance = 20 km

New time with increased speed:

Time = 20 km / 15 km/h

Time = (20)/(15) hr

Time = (4)/(3)hr

Time = 1.33 hrs

Time saved:

Time saved = 2 hrs - 1.33 hrs

Time saved = 0.67 hrs

Converting time saved to minutes:

Time saved = 0.67 hrs × 60 min/hr

Time saved = 40 min

**The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: A man can row at the speed of 8.5 km/h in still water. In a river running at the speed of 1.5 km/h, it takes him 51 minutes to row to a place and come back. How far (in km) is this place?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of man in still water = 8.5 km/h

Speed of river = 1.5 km/h

Total time taken = 51 minutes = 51/60 hours = 17/20 hours

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed downstream + Distance/Speed upstream

Speed downstream = Speed in still water + Speed of river

Speed upstream = Speed in still water - Speed of river

**Calculation:**

Speed downstream = 8.5 + 1.5 = 10 km/h

Speed upstream = 8.5 - 1.5 = 7 km/h

Let the distance to the place be "D".

Total time taken = (D / Speed downstream) + (D / Speed upstream)

⇒ 17/20 = D/10 + D/7

⇒ 17/20 = (7D + 10D) / (10 × 7)

⇒ 17/20 = 17D / 70

⇒ D = 3.5 km

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: The speed of the current is 4 km/hr. A motorboat goes 6 km upstream and back again to the starting point in 48 minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the motor of the sailor is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the current = 4 km/hr

Distance upstream = 6 km

Total time = 48 minutes = 48 / 60 hours = 4/5 hours

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the motor of the sailor = x km/hr

Speed upstream = (x - 4) km/hr

Speed downstream = (x + 4) km/hr

Total time = Time upstream + Time downstream

⇒ 4/5 = 6 / (x - 4) + 6 / (x + 4)

⇒ 4/5 = 6(x + 4) + 6(x - 4) / ((x - 4)(x + 4))

⇒ 4/5 = (6x + 24 + 6x - 24) / (x² - 16)

⇒ 4/5 = 12x / (x² - 16)

⇒ 4(x² - 16) = 60x

⇒ 4x² - 60x - 64 = 0

⇒ x² - 15x - 16 = 0

Factorize the quadratic equation:

⇒ (x - 16)(x + 1) = 0

⇒ x = 16 or x = -1

Since speed cannot be negative, x = 16 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: If the ratio of speed upstream and downstream is 5 : 7 and the speed of the stream is 6 m/sec, then what is the time taken by a boat to cover the total distance of 210 m both upstream and downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of speeds upstream and downstream = 5:7

Speed of the stream = 6 m/sec

Total distance = 210 m

**Formula used:**

Speed of boat in still water = dfrac{{Sum of upstream and downstream speeds}}{2}

Speed of stream = dfrac{{Difference of downstream and upstream speeds}}{2}

Time = dfrac{{Distance}}{{Speed}}

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the boat in still water = x m/sec.

Upstream speed = x - 6 m/sec

Downstream speed = x + 6 m/sec

Given upstream : downstream = 5 : 7

⇒ dfrac{x-6}{x+6} = dfrac{5}{7}

⇒ 7(x - 6) = 5(x + 6)

⇒ 7x - 42 = 5x + 30

⇒ 7x - 5x = 30 + 42

⇒ 2x = 72

⇒ x = 36 m/sec

Upstream speed = x - 6 = 36 - 6 = 30 m/sec

Downstream speed = x + 6 = 36 + 6 = 42 m/sec

Time upstream = dfrac{{Distance}}{{Speed}} = dfrac{210}{30} = 7 {sec}

Time downstream = dfrac{{Distance}}{{Speed}} = dfrac{210}{42} = 5 {sec}

Total time = Time upstream + Time downstream = 7 + 5 = 12 sec

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A person can complete a journey in 6 hours. He covers the first one-third part of the journey at the rate of 23 km/h and the remaining distance at the rate of 46 km/h. What is the total distance (in km) of his journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total time taken for the journey = 6 hours

Speed for the first one-third of the journey (v₁) = 23 km/h

Speed for the remaining two-thirds of the journey (v₂) = 46 km/h

**Calculation:**

Let the total distance of the journey be 3D km.

Distance of the first one-third part = (1/3) × 3D = D km

Distance of the remaining two-thirds part = 3D - D = 2D km

Time taken to cover the first one-third part (t₁) = Distance / Speed = (D)/(23) hours

Time taken to cover the remaining two-thirds part (t₂) = Distance / Speed = (2D)/(46) = (D)/(23) 

The total time taken for the journey is given as 6 hours.

Total Time = t₁ + t₂

6 = (D)/(23) + (D)/(23)

6 = (D + D)/(23)

2D = 6 × 23

2D = 138

D = 69 km

Total Distance = 3 × D = 3 × 69 = 207 km

**The total distance of his journey is 207 km.**

questions.question: A person can complete a journey in 9 hours. He covers the first one-third part of the journey at the rate of 10 km/h and the remaining distance at the rate of 20 km/h. What is the total distance of his journey (in km)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person can complete a journey in 9 hours.

First one-third of the journey at 10 km/h.

Remaining two-thirds of the journey at 20 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total Time = Time for first part + Time for second part

Let Total Distance = D km.

**Calculation:**

Total Time = 9 hours

Distance covered in the first part = D ÷ 3

Speed for the first part = 10 km/h

Time for the first part = (D ÷ 3) ÷ 10 = D ÷ 30

Distance covered in the second part = 2D ÷ 3

Speed for the second part = 20 km/h

Time for the second part = (2D ÷ 3) ÷ 20 = 2D ÷ 60 = D ÷ 30

Total Time = D ÷ 30 + D ÷ 30

⇒ 9 = (D ÷ 30) + (D ÷ 30)

⇒ 9 = 2D ÷ 30

⇒ D = (9 × 30) ÷ 2

⇒ D = 135 km

**∴ The total distance of the journey is 135 km. **

questions.question: A person can complete a journey in 24 hours. He covers the first one-third part of the journey at the rate of 42 km/h and the remaining distance at the rate of 12 km/h. What is the total distance(km) of his journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

A person can complete a journey in 24 hours.

First one-third of the journey is covered at 42 km/h.

Remaining two-thirds of the journey is covered at 12 km/h.

Formula used:

Total time = (Time for first part) + (Time for second part)

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculation:

Let total distance = D km.

First part of the journey = (1/3) × D = D/3 km.

Second part of the journey = (2/3) × D = 2D/3 km.

Time for first part = (D/3) ÷ 42 = D/(3 × 42) = D/126 hours.

Time for second part = (2D/3) ÷ 12 = 2D/(3 × 12) = 2D/36 = D/18 hours.

Total time = D/126 + D/18 = 24

LCM of 126 and 18 = 126

D/126 + 7D/126 = 24

⇒ (1D + 7D)/126 = 24

⇒ 8D / 126 = 24

⇒ 8D = 24 × 126 = 3024

⇒ D = 3024 ÷ 8 = 378

∴ The total distance of the journey is 378 km.

questions.question: Kavya has to reach Bhopal which is 1011 km away in 19 hours. His starting speed for 7 hours was 25 km/hr. For the next 152 km his speed was 19km/hr. By what speed he must travel now so as to reach Bhopal in decided time of 19 hours?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance to Bhopal = 1011 km

Total time to reach Bhopal = 19 hours

Calculation:

Journey Phase 1: Speed = 25 km/hr, Time = 7 hours

Distance covered in Phase 1 = Speed × Time = 25 km/hr × 7 hours = 175 km

Journey Phase 2: Distance covered = 152 km, Speed = 19 km/hr

Time taken in Phase 2 = Distance / Speed = 152 km / 19 km/hr = 8 hours

For the Remaining Journey:

Total distance covered so far = Distance in Phase 1 + Distance in Phase 2 = 175 km + 152 km = 327 km

Remaining distance to travel = Total distance - Total distance covered so far = 1011 km - 327 km = 684 km

Total time spent so far = Time in Phase 1 + Time in Phase 2 = 7 hours + 8 hours = 15 hours

Remaining time to reach Bhopal = Total time - Total time spent so far = 19 hours - 15 hours = 4 hours

Required speed for the remaining journey = Remaining distance / Remaining time

Required speed = 684 km / 4 hours = 171 km/hr

**∴ Kavya must travel at a speed of 171 km/hr to reach Bhopal in the decided time.**

questions.question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 5.4 km/h. The other one walks at 10.8 km/h. The train needs 5.1 and 6.8 seconds respectively to overtake them. What is the speed of the train if both the persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the first person (v₁) = 5.4 km/h

Speed of the second person (v₂) = 10.8 km/h

Time taken to overtake the first person (t₁) = 5.1 seconds

Time taken to overtake the second person (t₂) = 6.8 seconds

Both persons are walking in the same direction as the train.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of the faster object - Speed of the slower object (when moving in the same direction)

Distance = Relative speed × Time

The distance covered by the train to overtake each person is equal to the length of the train (L).

**Calculation:**

v₁ = 5.4 × (1000 / 3600) m/s = 5.4 × (5 / 18) m/s = 1.5 m/s

v₂ = 10.8 × (1000 / 3600) m/s = 10.8 × (5 / 18) m/s = 3 m/s

Let the speed of the train be vₜ m/s and the length of the train be L meters.

When overtaking the first person, the relative speed = (vₜ - 1.5) m/s.

Distance = Relative speed × Time

L = (vₜ - 1.5) × 5.1 (Equation 1)

When overtaking the second person, the relative speed = (vₜ - 3) m/s.

L = (vₜ - 3) × 6.8 (Equation 2)

Since the length of the train (L) is the same in both cases, we can equate Equation 1 and Equation 2:

(vₜ - 1.5) × 5.1 = (vₜ - 3) × 6.8

5.1vₜ - (1.5 × 5.1) = 6.8vₜ - (3 × 6.8)

5.1vₜ - 7.65 = 6.8vₜ - 20.4

20.4 - 7.65 = 6.8vₜ - 5.1vₜ

12.75 = 1.7vₜ

vₜ = 12.75 / 1.7

vₜ = 7.5 m/s = 7.5 × (18 / 5) km/h = 1.5 × 18 km/h = 27 km/h

**The speed of the train is 27 km/h.**

questions.question: A 280 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 5 km/h (in same direction) in 42 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another 500 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 43 km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train 1 (L1) = 280 m

Speed of Man (S_man) = 5 km/h

Time taken to overtake man (T1) = 42 seconds

Length of Train 2 (L2) = 500 m

Speed of Train 2 (S2) = 43 km/h (opposite direction)

**Calculation:**

When a train overtakes a man, the distance covered is the length of the train. The relative speed is (Speed of train - Speed of man).

Let the speed of Train 1 be S1 km/h.

Relative speed (Sᵣₑₗ₁) = (S1 - 5) km/h = (S1 - 5) × (5/18) m/s

Distance (L1) = 280 m

Time (T1) = 42 seconds

Using Distance = Speed × Time:

280 = (S1 - 5) × (5/18) × 42

280 = (S1 - 5) × (210/18)

280 = (S1 - 5) × (35/3)

(280 × 3) / 35 = S1 - 5

840 / 35 = S1 - 5

24 = S1 - 5

S1 = 24 + 5 = 29 km/h

Total distance to cross (D) = L1 + L2 = 280 + 500 = 780 m

Speed of Train 1 (S1) = 29 km/h

Speed of Train 2 (S2) = 43 km/h

Relative speed (Sᵣₑₗ₂) = S1 + S2 (since they are moving in opposite directions)

Sᵣₑₗ₂ = 29 km/h + 43 km/h = 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

Time taken (T2) = Total distance / Relative speed

T2 = 780 m / 20 m/s

T2 = 39 seconds

**∴ It will take 39 seconds for the first train to completely cross the second train.**

questions.question: A 275 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 6 km/h (in same direction) in 45 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another 280 m long train, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 26 km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A 275 m long train overtakes a man moving at a speed of 6 km/h (in the same direction) in 45 seconds.

Another train length = 280 m, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 26 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed of train - Speed of man

Relative speed (opposite direction) = Speed of train + Speed of other train

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Speed of man = 6 km/h = 6 × (5/18) m/s = 5/3 m/s

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed of train - Speed of man

⇒ (Speed of train - 5/3) m/s = Distance / Time

⇒ (Speed of train - 5/3) = 275 / 45

⇒ Speed of train = (275 / 45) + 5/3

⇒ Speed of train = 350 / 45 m/s = 7.78 m/s

Relative speed (opposite direction) = Speed of train + Speed of other train

Speed of other train = 26 km/h = 26 × (5/18) m/s = 7.22 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 7.78 + 7.22 = 15 m/s

Combined length of both trains = 275 m + 280 m = 555 m

Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 555 / 15 = 37 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Train A leaves station M at 7:35 AM and reaches station N at 2:35 PM on the same day. Train B leaves station N at 9:35 AM and reaches station M at 2:35 PM on the same day. Find the time when Trains A and B meet.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train A leaves station M at 7:35 AM and reaches station N at 2:35 PM, taking 7 hours to complete the journey.

Train B leaves station N at 9:35 AM and reaches station M at 2:35 PM, taking 5 hours to complete the journey.

Let the distance between stations M and N be D.

**Formula used:**

Time taken by Train A to meet Train B can be calculated by relative speed and position:

Distance covered by Train A + Distance covered by Train B = Total distance (D).

**Calculations:**

Speed of Train A (SA) = (D)/(7)

Speed of Train B (SB) = (D)/(5)

Train A starts at 7:35 AM, and Train B starts at 9:35 AM.

By the time Train B starts, Train A has already traveled for 2 hours.

Distance covered by Train A in 2 hours = (D)/(7) times 2 = (2D)/(7)

Remaining distance to be covered by both trains = (5D)/(7)

Relative speed of Train A and Train B = (D)/(7) + (D)/(5) = (12D)/(35)

Time taken for the trains to meet = frac{{Remaining distance}}{{Relative speed}} = (frac{5D)/(7)}{(12D)/(35)} = (5)/(7) times (35)/(12) = (25)/(12)

⇒ Time taken = 2 hours and 5 minutes.

Train B starts at 9:35 AM, so the meeting time = 9:35 AM + 2 hours and 5 minutes = 11:40 AM.

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Train A leaves station M at 7:40 AM and reaches station N at 2:40 PM on the same day. Train B leaves station N at 9:40 AM and reaches station M at 2:40 PM on the same day. Find the time when Trains A and B meet.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train A leaves station M at 7:40 AM and reaches station N at 2:40 PM.

Time taken by Train A (TA) = 2:40 PM - 7:40 AM = 7 hours.

Train B leaves station N at 9:40 AM and reaches station M at 2:40 PM.

Time taken by Train B (TB) = 2:40 PM - 9:40 AM = 5 hours.

**Calculations:**

Let the distance between station M and station N be D.

Speed of Train A (SA) = D / TA = D / 7

Speed of Train B (SB) = D / TB = D / 5

Train A starts at 7:40 AM. Train B starts at 9:40 AM.

Time difference in starting = 9:40 AM - 7:40 AM = 2 hours.

In these 2 hours, Train A covers a distance before Train B starts:

Distance covered by Train A in 2 hours = SA × 2 = (D / 7) × 2 = 2D / 7

Remaining distance between the trains when Train B starts = D - (2D / 7) = (7D - 2D) / 7 = 5D / 7

Now, both trains are moving towards each other from 9:40 AM. Their relative speed is:

Relative Speed (Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ) = SA + SB = (D / 7) + (D / 5)

⇒ Sᵣₑₗₐₜᵢvₑ = (5D + 7D) / 35 = 12D / 35

Time taken for them to meet (tₘₑₑₜ) after 9:40 AM = Remaining Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ tₘₑₑₜ = (5D / 7) / (12D / 35)

⇒ tₘₑₑₜ = (5D / 7) × (35 / 12D)

⇒ tₘₑₑₜ = (5 × 35) / (7 × 12)

⇒ tₘₑₑₜ = (5 × 5) / 12

⇒ tₘₑₑₜ = 25 / 12 hours

So, tₘₑₑₜ = 2 hours and 5 minutes

The trains meet 2 hours and 5 minutes after 9:40 AM.

Meeting Time = 9:40 AM + 2 hours 5 minutes = 11:45 AM

**∴ The time when Trains A and B meet is 11:45 AM.**

questions.question: In covering a distance of 90 km, Anirudh takes 8 hours more than Burhan. If Anirudh doubles his speed, then he would take 7 hour less than Burhan. Anirudh's speed is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 90 km

If Anirudh doubles his speed, he takes 7 hrs less than Burhan

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

Burhan's speed = x km/h

Anirudh's speed = y km/h

So, Burhan's time = 90 ÷ x

Anirudh's time = 90 ÷ y

Anirudh's time when speed is doubled = 90 ÷ (2y)

**Using condition 1:**

⇒ 90 ÷ y = 90 ÷ x + 8 ...(i)

**Using condition 2:**

⇒ 90 ÷ (2y) = 90 ÷ x − 7 ...(ii)

**Multiply (i) by 2:**

⇒ 180 ÷ y = 180 ÷ x + 16

**Subtract (ii) from this:**

(180 ÷ y − 90 ÷ (2y)) = (180 ÷ x + 16) − (90 ÷ x − 7)

⇒ (180 − 90) ÷ (2y) = (180 − 90) ÷ x + (16 + 7)

⇒ 90 ÷ (2y) = 90 ÷ x + 23

**Now substitute:**

Let’s solve equation (i):

90 ÷ y = 90 ÷ x + 8

⇒ 90 ÷ x = 90 ÷ y − 8

Now use in equation (ii):

⇒ 90 ÷ (2y) = (90 ÷ y − 8) − 7 = 90 ÷ y − 15

⇒ 90 ÷ (2y) = 90 ÷ y − 15

Multiply both sides by 2:

⇒ 90 ÷ y = 180 ÷ y − 30

⇒ 90 ÷ y − 180 ÷ y = −30

⇒ − 90 ÷ y = −30

⇒ y = 3

**∴ Anirudh's speed is 3 km/h.**
